purpose: Implements issue #228 by wiring the previously underutilized event bus into the pipeline: ReviewEngine now publishes typed pipeline lifecycle events (review/fix/audit/analyze/explain/conversation started+completed) via a guarded publishEvent helper, and adds a config-driven JSONL LoggingSubscriber, a TelemetrySubscriber, and pluggable subscriber registration wired into the GitHub Action.
riskRationale: No crashes or security-critical holes were found, but the PR silently drops learning-store quality telemetry by default: the recordQuality write removed from ReviewEngine.recordTelemetry is replaced by a TelemetrySubscriber that neither the app nor the action registers, so /metrics reports fall to zero. The Probot app also never passes the event bus to six of seven subscriber factories (and never calls registerEventSubscribers), so the headline feature is only realized for reviews there; the pluggable dynamic-import loader cannot resolve relative paths in the ncc-bundled action; and pnpm lint fails on 7 Biome formatting errors in touched files, blocking CI.
breakingChanges: Learning-store quality recording removed from ReviewEngine.recordTelemetry; the TelemetrySubscriber replacement is never registered, so review_quality rows (durationMs/tokensUsed/scores) are no longer written by default in either the action or the app.

The 'review.completed' event category changes from 'internal' to 'pipeline' and its payload gains timestamp/modelUsed/durationMs/tokensUsed; external event-bus consumers depending on the old category or payload shape must adapt.

text: The PR takes a sound architectural direction — strongly-typed pipeline lifecycle events, a gracefully-degrading publishEvent, removal of the duplicated review.completed publish, and opt-in config-driven logging/pluggable subscribers. However the integration is incomplete and regressive as shipped: the TelemetrySubscriber meant to replace the deleted learning-store write is never registered (silently dropping quality/latency/token telemetry), the app wires the bus only into the review subscriber so fix/audit/analyze/explain/conversation events never fire there, the pluggable dynamic-import loader is inert inside the bundled action, and no tests were added for any of the new functionality.

reasoning: Blocking before merge: the learning-store quality telemetry regression (TelemetrySubscriber never registered) and the unwired app subscribers must be fixed, and the pluggable loader's ncc-incompatible path resolution and the awaited publish-on-hot-path should be addressed. All of these are small, low-risk wiring and robustness changes.

message: publishEvent is well-guarded: it no-ops without a bus and wraps publish in try/catch with a logger.warn, so a missing or failing event bus can never break the review/fix pipeline — a clean instance of the repo's graceful-degradation convention.

The PipelineEventPayloadMap keyed by PIPELINE_EVENT_TYPES constants with Omit<..., 'timestamp'> gives fully type-checked, self-documenting payloads per event type with no 'any', and publishEvent's generic signature enforces that each event carries exactly its documented fields.

Moving review.completed publishing out of the review subscriber and into the engine removes the duplicated/divergent manual event construction, keeps lifecycle events in one place, and guarantees a consistent payload shape for downstream consumers like MetaReviewSubscriber.

eventLogging and eventSubscribers are validated both in validateConfig and the Zod schemas with sane defaults and graceful filtering of malformed entries, so misconfigured YAML degrades safely instead of crashing.

The learningStore.recordQuality block was removed from recordTelemetry, and the intended replacement — the new TelemetrySubscriber — is exported from lib/src/index.ts but never instantiated or registered anywhere: app/src/subscribers/index.ts does not register it, and action/src/index.ts's registerEventSubscribers only registers LoggingSubscriber plus user-configured pluggable entries. Because getTelemetryStats and getLatencyStats in lib/src/learning/db/sql-adapter.ts read duration_ms/tokens_used from the review_quality table, /metrics reports (avg review duration, total tokens, review counts) silently fall to zero in both the GitHub Action and the Probot App after this merges — a functional regression that defeats the purpose of the PR.
suggestion: Register a TelemetrySubscriber on the bus wherever a LearningStore is available (in both the app's registerSubscribers and the action's run), or keep a direct recordQuality write in recordTelemetry as a fallback when no bus is attached, so telemetry behavior is preserved regardless of wiring.

message: Six subscriber factories (fix, audit, analyze, auto-analyze, explain, conversation) now accept an eventBus parameter, but registerSubscribers never passes the app's bus to them — only createReviewSubscriber gets it — so no fix/audit/analyze/explain/conversation pipeline events are ever emitted in the Probot app. Separately, app/src/index.ts never calls registerEventSubscribers, so the new eventLogging/eventSubscribers config options are silently ignored in the app, leaving the bulk of this PR's plumbing dead code.
suggestion: Pass the shared bus into every subscriber factory in registerSubscribers and call registerEventSubscribers(bus, config.eventLogging, config.eventSubscribers) at app startup so the app honors the new config options like the action does.
suggestionCode:
createFixSubscriber(rateLimiter, bus),
createAuditSubscriber(rateLimiter, bus),
createAnalyzeSubscriber(rateLimiter, bus),
createAutoAnalyzeSubscriber(rateLimiter, bus),
createExplainSubscriber(rateLimiter, bus),
createConversationSubscriber(learningStore, rateLimiter, bus),

message: resolveSubscriberModule uses a bare runtime dynamic import(modulePath) with no restriction on where the path resolves. Relative paths like './my-subscriber.js' resolve against lib's own module directory (or the ncc bundle in the shipped action, which does not bundle non-literal dynamic imports) rather than the repo checkout, so repo-relative config paths silently fail to load and the feature is effectively inert in its only wired caller. It is also an arbitrary code-execution primitive: the config is loaded from the audited repository, so a hostile repo could point eventSubscribers[].path at an absolute module path and execute code inside the runner, bypassing the command allowlist that constrains other config-driven execution.
suggestion: Resolve relative paths against the working directory (process.cwd()) before importing, require the resolved path to be inside the repo checkout, and document eventSubscribers as trusted first-party config (or gate the feature behind an explicit opt-in flag).

message: sub.name is mutated on the object returned by dynamic import(). Node caches imports: for a CJS subscriber module the mutation leaks into the shared module.exports, and for an ESM module the frozen namespace object throws a TypeError outside the try/catch in resolveSubscriberModule, failing the whole startup block. Two config entries pointing at the same module path also resolve to the same cached object, so the second registration reuses the first entry's name (the dedup guard no longer triggers) and the same subscriber instance is registered twice — every event handled twice and circuit-breaker/health state collides under one name.
suggestion: Do not mutate the resolved object — build a shallow copy carrying the display name and de-duplicate registrations by module path.

message: publishEvent awaits eventBus.publish() inline on the critical path of every pipeline stage. EventBus.publish runs each subscriber with SUBSCRIBER_TIMEOUT_MS = 600_000ms, and this PR explicitly enables pluggable third-party subscribers — so one slow/hung subscriber can stall every review/fix/audit/analyze stage for up to 10 minutes per event (two awaited publishes per stage), contradicting the graceful-degradation intent stated in the code comment.
suggestion: Treat event publishing as non-critical observability: fire-and-forget with a catch (or await with a short bounded timeout) so subscriber latency can never block the pipeline.

message: handle() writes review_quality rows with actionabilityScore/accuracyScore/coverageScore/consistencyScore all hardcoded to 0 for every *completed event (review, fix, audit, analyze, explain, conversation). These rows feed aggregateMetrics and getTelemetryStats in lib/src/learning/db/sql-adapter.ts, which average the score columns and count every row as a 'review' without filtering zeros — so enabling this subscriber drags average quality scores toward 0 and inflates totalReviews/avgTokensPerReview. getQualityTrends filters zero rows, but the metrics-report paths do not.
suggestion: Only write quality rows when genuine scores exist: gate the recordQuality call on quality-bearing payload fields (or drop it and persist durationMs/tokensUsed through a telemetry-only path), or add the same zero-row filter getQualityTrends uses to aggregateMetrics/getTelemetryStats.
suggestionCode:
const { actionabilityScore, accuracyScore, coverageScore, consistencyScore } = payload;
if (!actionabilityScore && !accuracyScore && !coverageScore && !consistencyScore) return;

message: No tests were added or updated for the new functionality (publishEvent, LoggingSubscriber, TelemetrySubscriber, registerEventSubscribers, the eventLogging/eventSubscribers config schemas), and the removal of the recordQuality call in recordTelemetry has no coverage — which is exactly how the telemetry regression above shipped undetected.
suggestion: Add unit tests covering: publishEvent payload/timestamp construction, LoggingSubscriber writing well-formed JSONL and tolerating write failures, TelemetrySubscriber skipping events without a PR number and recording only when data exists, registerEventSubscribers honoring enabled/disabled config and skipping unloadable/bad modules, and a regression test asserting recordTelemetry still persists quality metrics when no bus is attached.

message: pnpm lint fails with 7 Biome formatting errors, all in files changed by this PR (commands.ts, auto-analyze.ts, conversation.ts, fix.ts, config.ts, engine.ts, register-event-subscribers.ts). CI runs pnpm lint, so this blocks the build and contradicts the PR's claim that the fix was verified with lint.
suggestion: Run pnpm exec biome check --write on the changed files and re-verify with pnpm lint before merge.

message: ERROR_OCCURRED and CONFIG_CHANGED are declared in PIPELINE_EVENT_TYPES (with payload interfaces defined) but no code path ever publishes them — dead/aspirational types that inflate the API surface and imply capabilities that do not exist, while the LoggingSubscriber's wildcard documentation implies config/error events exist.
suggestion: Either emit error.occurred from the engine's error/throw paths (it already logs the same information), or remove the unused constants and payload interfaces until they are actually published.

message: Engine-published events never set the repo field on the GitHubEvent envelope (only type/category/payload/timestamp/prNumber), whereas the review subscriber this replaces used to publish repo: event.repo. The JSONL event log and any repo-aware consumer therefore lose repository context for all pipeline events, making audit logs harder to attribute across repos.
suggestion: Include repo (derived from the adapter/PR context) in the event envelope in publishEvent so pipeline events carry owner/repo like webhook events do.

message: Analyze/explain/audit events carry issueNumber (and category/targetDir) in the payload, but publishEvent sets the top-level prNumber from eventPayload.prNumber, which is undefined for these events. Downstream consumers cannot correlate such events to a PR/issue via event.prNumber, and a registered TelemetrySubscriber would skip them entirely (its early return checks prNumber) despite subscribing to their .completed types.
suggestion: Map issueNumber to prNumber when publishing analyze/explain/audit events (GitHub issues and PRs share the same numbering space), or restrict TelemetrySubscriber's subscribedEvents to events that always carry a prNumber.

message: LoggingSubscriber subscribes to wildcard '*' and writes every event via JSON.stringify with no rotation or size cap. In the action the autofix loop can git-add the whole working tree, risking accidental commits of .opencode/events.ndjson containing full review summaries and raw webhook payloads (sender login/email, PR/issue/comment bodies, repository metadata); over time the unbounded file also risks filling the runner disk.
suggestion: Subscribe only to pipeline-category events or redact/truncate sensitive payload fields before serializing; cap or rotate the log past a size threshold; and ensure the log path is gitignored or excluded from autofix commits.

message: handle() calls fs.mkdir on every published event even though the directory already exists after the first append, adding a filesystem syscall per event on the hot path.
suggestion: Ensure the log directory once (lazily on first event or in the constructor) and keep the per-event mkdir inside the try/catch only as a re-creation safety net.

message: Two defensive gaps: the catch block is empty, so learning-store write failures are completely invisible (no log line, and LearningStore.recordQuality already swallows internally, so the outer try/catch is redundant), and const payload = event.payload as PipelineEventPayload is an unverified cast from unknown dereferenced outside the try/catch — a malformed future event would throw into the EventBus error path instead of degrading gracefully.
suggestion: Log a warning (e.g. new Logger('TelemetrySubscriber').warn(...)) before swallowing store errors, and validate the payload shape (typeof payload === 'object' && payload !== null) or read fields via optional chaining before the early returns.

message: autoCloseReason is set to the constant 'closed' based on state?.alreadyClosed after the turn, losing the actual close reason (e.g. 'max_turns'/'limit') that shouldAutoClose returns via decision.reason, and it labels any turn on an already-closed thread as 'closed' even when nothing meaningful happened.
suggestion: Capture the real reason from the auto-close decision in runTurn and propagate it to the completed event instead of the hardcoded 'closed'.

message: review.completed is now published inside engine.reviewPR before the handler posts the review and stores findings, and publishEvent awaits all subscribers synchronously — MetaReviewSubscriber (which can trigger a meta-review model run) now runs before findings are persisted and can delay the user-facing review post. Previously the event fired after the review was fully posted.
suggestion: Publish completion events after the handler finishes (or make completion publishes non-blocking) so heavy subscribers cannot delay the review post or observe unpersisted state.

message: AUDIT_COMPLETED/ANALYZE_COMPLETED/EXPLAIN_COMPLETED are published from 3-4 near-identical branches (engine.ts:1006,1022,1036; 1095,1108,1118,1128; 1299,1311,1320), each repeating getLastTelemetry() + publishEvent boilerplate — easy to desync, and any future branch added without the publish silently misses an event.
suggestion: Wrap each method body in try/finally and publish the COMPLETED event once in the finally block, or extract a small publishCompleted(type, extra) helper so all exit paths emit exactly one event.
